evals.prompt:
Run a candidate audit for an HSE Specialist role at Orion Automotive in Kingston, Ontario. Orion Lighting and Orion Interiors are Orion Automotive divisions. Must-haves: automotive manufacturing, ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 exposure, incident investigations, Ontario safety knowledge, and realistic Kingston logistics. Salary is $75K-$85K. Clean the repeated headers and duplicates, audit every unique person once, and return a concise ranked table. Public profiles only; do not invent contact data. Input rows:
Name | Current title/company | Location | Public evidence
Name | Current title/company | Location | Public evidence
Synthetic Candidate E | HSE Coordinator, Orion Lighting | Kingston | ISO 45001 and 14001 internal auditor; investigations
Synthetic Candidate A | EHS Lead, Thermo Systems | Belleville | automotive manufacturing; ISO 45001/14001; WSIB and investigations
Synthetic Candidate A | EHS Lead, Thermo Systems | Belleville | duplicate row
Synthetic Candidate C | Global VP EHS, MotionWorks | Toronto | enterprise automotive EHS leader
Synthetic Candidate D | Safety Committee Member, Northstar Retail | Kingston | JHSC member; no manufacturing evidence
Synthetic Candidate B | HSE Coordinator, MetalForm Canada | Oshawa | automotive; incident investigations; ISO status unconfirmed
evals.expected_output: A deduplicated candidate table that excludes Synthetic Candidate E as a current client-group employee, does not recommend excluded or overqualified people first, ranks eligible candidates from supplied evidence, and lists concise verification gaps.
expectations: The candidate table contains exactly one row for each of the five unique people and no repeated header row.
Synthetic Candidate E is marked Excluded because Orion Lighting belongs to the hiring client group, and Synthetic Candidate E is absent from the top recommendations.
Synthetic Candidate A is the first eligible recommendation based on direct automotive HSE, ISO 45001/14001, WSIB, investigations, and plausible Belleville-to-Kingston logistics.
Synthetic Candidate C is not recommended ahead of plausible specialist-level candidates because the Global VP role creates a material seniority and compensation mismatch.
The output uses the required candidate columns and includes exclusions, top recommendations, and concise verification questions.
The output does not invent email addresses, phone numbers, credentials, or experience beyond the supplied evidence.

evals.prompt:
Audit this synthetic BD prospect list for a manufacturing recruitment campaign. Target accounts are Ontario automotive suppliers. Best contacts are plant leaders, HR/talent leaders, or operational executives with evidence of hiring or expansion. Existing Client Automotive Inc. is excluded. Target-account employees are desired and must not be rejected merely because they work there. Return one concise prospect-priority table, exclusions, top three, and only necessary verification questions. Public profiles only.
Name | Role/company | Location | Signal
Synthetic Prospect A | Plant Manager, Example Thermal Systems | Belleville | company posted 18 skilled-trades openings
Synthetic Prospect B | HR Director, Example MotionWorks | Guelph | company announced a new production line
Synthetic Prospect C | Software Developer, Example MotionWorks | Toronto | no hiring authority shown
Synthetic Prospect A | Plant Manager, Example Thermal Systems | Belleville | duplicate
Synthetic Prospect D | Talent Acquisition Manager, Existing Client Automotive Inc. | Aurora | active hiring posts
Synthetic Prospect E | Operations Director, Example AutoStamp | Cambridge | role verified; no current growth signal
Header Name | Role/company | Location | Signal
evals.expected_output: A deduplicated prospect table that keeps target-account employees eligible, excludes the Existing Client Automotive Inc. contact and irrelevant software developer, and separates commercial priority from evidence confidence.
expectations: The prospect table contains exactly one row for each of the five unique people and no repeated header row.
Synthetic Prospect A and Synthetic Prospect B remain eligible and rank above lower-signal prospects because target-account employees are desired.
Synthetic Prospect D is marked Excluded because Existing Client Automotive Inc. is an existing-client exclusion, despite the hiring signal.
Synthetic Prospect C is rejected or placed last because the software role has no shown staffing-buying authority.
Synthetic Prospect E is not rated High because no current growth or hiring signal is supplied.
The output uses the required prospect columns, separates priority from confidence, and does not invent contact data or business signals.

evals.prompt: Use the sourcing export workflow. From the approved JSON file provided in the task workspace, create both a generic candidate CSV and a Loxo-ready candidate CSV in the specified outputs directory. Remove the repeated header and duplicate profile. Do not import anything into Loxo. Verify headers and row counts, then save a short result summary as result.md. Input file: approved_rows.json.
evals.expected_output: Two CSV files with exact generic and Loxo headers, three unique data rows, safe values, and a result.md confirming output paths, headers, and counts.
expectations: The run creates one generic CSV, one Loxo-ready CSV, and result.md in the outputs directory.
The generic CSV header exactly matches Full Name, Title, Company, Location, LinkedIn, Status, Fit/Priority, Confidence, Evidence, Gaps/Risks, Notes.
The Loxo CSV header exactly matches First Name, Last Name, Full Name, Title, Company, Location, LinkedIn, Tags, Notes.
Each CSV contains exactly three unique data rows after removing one repeated header and one duplicate Synthetic Candidate A profile.
No Loxo import or external write occurs; the skill only prepares files.
result.md reports both output paths, verifies both headers, and states the exported row count.

evals.prompt: Map the supplied synthetic open roles for Synthetic Candidate H. Use the candidate's explicit preferences as hard decision inputs, not optional notes. Candidate: Senior Accountant at Example Foods. Wants Senior Accountant, Accounting Manager, or Assistant Controller roles in manufacturing; Toronto-west through Guelph; hybrid at least two days per week; minimum $105K; no relocation; no night shift. Current employer Example Foods must be excluded. Roles: Controller, Example Foods, Guelph, $130K, hybrid 2 days, manufacturing; Senior Accountant, Example MotionWorks, Cambridge, $110K, hybrid 2 days, automotive manufacturing; Plant Accountant, Example AutoStamp, Windsor, $115K, onsite, automotive; Assistant Controller, Example RetailCo, Toronto, $120K, hybrid 3 days, retail; Accounting Manager, Example FormTech, Milton, $100K, hybrid 2 days, manufacturing. Return the preference-aware opportunity map, best opportunities, exclusions, candidate questions, and search boundary. Do not apply or write to any system.
evals.expected_output: A job map that ranks Example MotionWorks first, treats Example RetailCo as an industry-adjacent possibility, and rejects or excludes roles that violate current-employer, location/work-model, or minimum-compensation preferences.
expectations: The output uses the required candidate-opportunity table columns and covers all five roles exactly once.
Example MotionWorks Senior Accountant ranks first and is Strong because title, manufacturing, geography, hybrid schedule, and compensation align.
Example Foods Controller is Excluded because it is the candidate's current employer, despite otherwise attractive terms.
Example AutoStamp Plant Accountant is rejected or excluded because Windsor and onsite work violate explicit location, relocation, and hybrid preferences.
Example FormTech Accounting Manager is rejected or excluded because $100K is below the explicit $105K minimum.
Example RetailCo Assistant Controller is Possible or Stretch, not Strong, because title, geography, hybrid, and pay align but industry preference does not.
The output includes best opportunities, exclusions, candidate questions, and an internal-role search boundary without applying or writing to any system.
